subject: Compliance orchestration: ISO scope, FedRAMP readiness & evidence asks
messages:
From: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@acme-fin.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acme-fin.com
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick: ISO scope & FedRAMP posture questions ahead of intake

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the demo earlier this week — Acme's security team is prepping our third-party intake and we have a few clarification requests to scope our risk assessment and upcoming evidence request. Could you confirm the following items so I can share with our auditors: 

1) ISO 27001: do you currently plan to include the Redwood Hosted API surface (public hosted endpoints) in the initial scope or is the first certification effort targeted at Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) only? If mixed, can you provide a proposed scope statement?

2) FedRAMP readiness: do you have an internal target for a FedRAMP low/moderate program (timeline or readiness score)? Any recent pre-audit runs or gap assessments we can review?

3) SIG/CAIQ: what is the expected format and cadence for the questionnaire and evidence intake? Will you accept a sample-based evidence window (e.g., 30-day snapshots) or do you require continuous export extracts for logs and KMS/HSM assertions?

4) KMS/HSM and key rotation: is there a documented KMS integration architecture we can reference (customer-managed keys for Private deployments)?

5) Audit window: what is your team's typical lead time to respond to an auditor's request for live evidence (logs, config snapshots, access lists)?

If you can send a short summary and any sample artifacts, that would be great — otherwise let's book a 30-min sync next week.

Appreciate it,
Oliver
Senior Security Engineer
Acme Financial

[Attachment: intake-questions-template.xlsx]
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@acme-fin.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: ISO scope & FedRAMP posture questions ahead of intake

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear list. Looping in our compliance and infra leads to confirm specifics. We'll put together a concise summary and attach sample artifacts. Quick answers up-front:

- ISO 27001: we intend to include Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) in the first certification bundle, with a documented annex covering the hosted API surface as an out-of-scope service but with compensating controls. We can share the draft scope doc.
- FedRAMP: we don't have a formal FedRAMP program started, but we have a maturity roadmap and recent gap scan (Q2 2026). We can share the gap assessment and a readiness scorecard.
- SIG/CAIQ: we typically provide a completed CAIQ/SIG matrix and accept sample-based evidence for logs (30-day snapshots) for most controls; for cryptographic controls we provide KMS/HSM architecture diagrams and rotation policies.
- KMS/HSM: customer-managed keys are supported for Private deployments; we have a KMS integration reference doc and rotation/playbook.
- Audit window: standard turnaround for non-sensitive artifact requests is 5 business days; for live log exports/accesses we aim for 7-10 business days depending on scope and legal approvals.

I'll coordinate attachments and a proposed 30-min slot.

Thanks,
Tessa
Director, Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: ISO27001-scope-draft.md]
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: ISO scope & FedRAMP posture questions ahead of intake

Tessa — added a few granular notes for the summary to Oliver: 

- ISO scope: propose language: "Certification boundary will include Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem components). Redwood Hosted API endpoints will be cataloged as an external-facing service with control mappings and compensating controls; sample evidentiary artifacts will be provided where applicable."
- Evidence types: for SIG we provide completed matrix + attachments where required; for CAIQ we provide a mapping sheet + sample snapshot exports. For logs we can provide 30-day SIEM snapshots (JSON/CSV) and a sample CloudTrail-style export for control verification.
- KMS: Priyom can attach the KMS reference—call out support for AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and an HSM-backed option for on-prem. Include key rotation policy and separation-of-duties doc.
- Audit window: ctrl owners should be pre-identified; we'll commit to a 7-business-day SLA for most evidence pulls if the request lists control IDs up front. Anything requiring forensic timelines or eDiscovery might be longer.

I'll add the suggested doc names to the attachments list and we can redact internal-only fields before sending.

-rishi
Head of Compliance Engineering
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@acme-fin.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: ISO scope & FedRAMP posture questions ahead of intake

Oliver — attaching the CAIQ/Control mapping sample and a short readme. A few specifics: 

- CAIQ: we provide a completed CAIQ spreadsheet and a mapping file (control -> artifact). For high-risk controls (cryptography, privileged access) we include configuration snapshots and operator runbooks.
- Evidence cadence: for initial intake we do a one-off snapshot package plus the mapping; subsequent auditor asks can be handled via scheduled snapshot windows (we've used 30-day rolling windows with enterprise customers).
- KMS/HSM: see the attached architecture diagram. For Private deployments where customers bring their own KMS, we provide a short integration checklist (keys-in-transit, key identifiers, rotation cadence).

Let me know if you want us to include example logs (we'll sanitize) or just the export format.

[Attachment: CAIQ-sample-mapping.xlsx]

- Priyom
Security Architect
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@acme-fin.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: ISO scope & FedRAMP posture questions ahead of intake

Hi Oliver — following up with a concise package and next steps. Attached are: 
- SIG_2026-request.pdf (completed SIG summary and high-level narrative)
- CAIQ-sample-mapping.xlsx (control -> artifact mapping + sample filenames)
- ISO27001-scope-draft.md (proposed boundary language and annex for Hosted API)

Short answers (recap):
- ISO 27001 scope: Redwood Private is the primary certification target. Hosted API will be documented as an external service with documented compensating controls and sampling for audit evidence.
- FedRAMP: no formal FedRAMP program yet; we have a Q2 2026 gap assessment and a readiness roadmap (we can share the scorecard in a redacted form).
- SIG/CAIQ cadence: initial completed questionnaires + 30-day sample snapshots for logs; cryptographic controls will have architecture diagrams + key rotation policies.
- KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed keys for Private; reference architecture included. For Hosted API customers we offer a managed key option and can discuss HSM-backed options for enterprise purchases.
- Audit window: we aim for 5-10 business days depending on artifact complexity and legal approvals; please include control IDs in requests to speed triage.

I'd like to propose a 30-minute call to walk through the attachments and agree a formal evidence intake template. Here are some options: Wed 9/30 10:00-10:30 PT or Thu 10/1 11:00-11:30 PT.

Best,
Tessa
Director, Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: SIG_2026-request.pdf, CAIQ-sample-mapping.xlsx, ISO27001-scope-draft.md]
